title: API Gateway with JWT and Cloud Run
summary: The gateway's OpenAPI spec says which token issuer and audience to accept. Valid requests go on to Cloud Run with a Google-signed ID token for the gateway's own service account, the only identity allowed to invoke the service.
notes: The API config's OpenAPI spec lists the trusted issuer (x-google-issuer), its key set (x-google-jwks_uri) and the allowed audiences (x-google-audiences). The gateway rejects a token that doesn't match before the backend sees it.
Each API config names a backend service account. The gateway mints a Google-signed ID token for it, with the backend URL as the audience, and calls Cloud Run with that token.

Because the gateway's token takes the Authorization header, it moves the caller's original token to X-Forwarded-Authorization. A backend that reads the user from it should trust that header only from the gateway.
Grant roles/run.invoker on the one Cloud Run service to the gateway's service account only, and don't allow unauthenticated invocations. IAM is what keeps callers from going around the gateway.
API keys in API Gateway identify the calling project, not the user. For OAuth policies, token introspection and fuller API management, Google's other gateway is Apigee.
